meta.title: Policy | Audit & Report
meta.description: The node policy of Audit & Report: backup, autostart and recovery objective of each guest, the role of each storage and the thresholds of the checks.

header.title: Policy
header.description: The policy declares what no inspection can deduce: what each guest and storage is for and the thresholds the checks apply.

calloutInfo.title: With no declaration, the report describes; with one, it assesses
calloutInfo.body: An assessment sees what the host does, not what it is for. A guest without a backup whose purpose is not declared is reported as an observation. If its backup is declared required, the same absence is reported as a warning. Nothing has to be declared.

figure.alt: Policy view with the guests, the storage and the thresholds of the node
figure.caption: The Policy view.

sections.title: Guests
sections.intro: Each VM and LXC of the node has three fields. A value left as default takes the general value, shown next to it.

rows: A missing backup is a warning when it is required, an observation when it is not stated, and it is left out of the count when it is not required.
Whether the guest has to start with the host.
The maximum acceptable age of the last backup.

sections.title: Storage

blocks.p: An unreachable storage is reported as critical when it is declared essential or serves a running guest, as a warning when its role is not stated, and as an observation when it is declared optional.

sections.intro: Each storage of the node is declared Essential, Optional or Not stated.

sections.title: Thresholds
sections.intro: An empty threshold uses the shipped value, shown as its placeholder.

items: Storage capacity review (%) and thin pool fill review (%).
Thin overprovisioning ratio and memory overcommit ratio.
Backup age fallback (days) and schedule grace (ratio).
Disk service life (hours) and recent disk error window (days).
Lynis report age (days) and package index age (days).
Filesystem space review (%) and filesystem inode review (%).

blocks.p: The declaration is validated and saved atomically in /usr/local/share/proxmenux/audit_policy.json. Each save carries a revision: if the declaration changed in another session, the draft is not saved and the view offers to reload the saved declaration.

calloutWarning.title: The policy is never inferred
calloutWarning.body: ProxMenux adds no requirement on its own. An empty field keeps the shipped value or stays not stated, and a partial declaration only affects the elements it names.
